newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end lower as longs liquidate.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end lower as longs liquidate.

text.p: Tokyo yen-based precious metal futures ended mostly lower on Tuesday, with the nearby December gold and platinum contracts coming under particularly heavy pressure from long liquidation by individual investors ahead of Wednesday's expiry, traders said.
The selling also dragged down bullion prices, which extended New York's modest losses overnight in otherwise featureless trade.
TOCOM most-active October 1997 gold ended three yen lower at 1,331 yen per gram, while nearby December was off five yen at 1,347.
TOCOM October platinum ended off one yen at 1,341 yen per gram, while nearby December tumbled eight yen to 1,350.
October palladium settled two lower at 428 yen per gram while October silver was up 0.4 at 178.4 yen per 10 grams.
The foreign exchange market offered little direction to TOCOM traders, with the yen/dollar rate holding close to Monday's levels.
In the bullion market, spot gold settled at $367.45/75 an ounce, down from New York's closing quote of $367.80/30 and Tokyo's Monday close of $368.20/50.
Several traders expected the gold market to retain its weak tone through the year-end holidays, although one European trader said support was likely to hold at $366 to $367.
"Once tomorrow (the TOCOM expiry) passes, the selling pressure will disappear and there won't be much movement through the year end," he said.

Another trader stressed, however, that the market remains in a bearish mood. "It's sensitive to bearish factors and oblivious to bullish factors," he said, noting that gold could not manage a bounce even during recent stock market declines.
